page: The UpCloud PREMIUM-1xCPU-1GB is an entry-level virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9575F processor. It features 1 shared vCPU operating at 2.0 GHz, backed by 1.0 GB of RAM and 25 GB of local SSD storage. The CPU architecture includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, vector neural network instructions, and hardware-accelerated cryptography, though it lacks advanced matrix extensions.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast in performance capabilities. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is positioned in the top tier, demonstrating the high efficiency of the underlying AMD EPYC core. However, due to the single-core shared allocation, multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU scores fall into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is a significant bottleneck, with Passmark memory and database operations scoring in the bottom 10%, and read-only memory bandwidth categorized as weak.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server provides a low-cost entry point to modern AMD EPYC hardware, making it suitable for resource-constrained environments where high memory density is not required. Given the 1.0 GB memory limitation and weak database benchmark results, it is not suited for database hosting or memory-intensive applications. Appropriate workloads include lightweight web serving, basic microservices, software development testing, and simple automation scripts.
